title: Lang surjectivity for connected affine groups over a finite field
statement: Let $k$ be a finite field [def-weil-field, def-weil-finite-field-q-elements], put $q=|k|$, and let $\bar k$ be an algebraic closure [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $G$ be an affine $k$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and connected [def-weil-connected-scheme]. Write $C=\Gamma(G,\mathcal O_G)$ and identify $G(\bar k)$ with the $k$-algebra homomorphisms $C\to\bar k$. Let $\sigma:G(\bar k)\to G(\bar k)$ send $x$ to $(c\mapsto x(c)^q)$, the action of arithmetic Frobenius [def-weil-frobenius-substitution]. Then the map $G(\bar k)\to G(\bar k)$, $g\mapsto g^{-1}\sigma(g)$, is surjective: for every $h\in G(\bar k)$ there exists $g\in G(\bar k)$ with $g^{-1}\sigma(g)=h$. No reductivity or commutativity hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Section 17.k, Corollary 17.97, printed p.383, and Theorem 17.96. The displayed map there is x F(x^{-1}); substituting x=g^{-1} gives g^{-1}F(g). On algebraic-closure points F is arithmetic Frobenius, as specified immediately before Definition 17.95, p.382.

proof.text: Put $K=\bar k$ and $H=G\times_kK$. The identity is a $k$-rational section, so [lem-sbc-connected-rational-point-geometrically-connected] makes $H$ connected. The coordinate algebra of $H$ is $C\otimes_kK$, so it is affine. It is of finite type by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]. It is smooth by [lem-sfb-scheme-lfp-smooth-flat-base-change]: the original smooth morphism is locally finitely presented, and $K/k$ is flat, since a vector-space basis makes tensoring with $K$ a direct sum of copies of the identity functor on $k$-vector spaces. Affineness makes $H$ separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated]. Smoothness gives regularity by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular], and connectedness and [lem-sc-regular-connected-integral] give integrality, in particular irreducibility. Finally $d=\dim H$ is a finite nonnegative integer: apply [lem-kun-finite-type-local-dimension] at the identity and [lem-ag-group-identity-local-dimension] to identify its local dimension with $\dim H$.

source.place: Theorem 17.96 and Corollary 17.97, printed p.383; Proposition 1.66, pp.27–28.

proof.text: The $k$-algebra endomorphism $C\to C$, $c\mapsto c^q$, defines a $k$-group endomorphism $F:G\to G$. Indeed $q$ is a positive power of the characteristic, $a^q=a$ for $a\in k$, and raising to $q$ commutes with the coproduct, counit and antipode. Base change gives a $K$-group endomorphism $F:H\to H$. Its action on $H(K)=G(K)$ is exactly $\sigma$, since evaluation of $c^q$ is $x(c)^q$; coefficients in $K$ are fixed in this base-changed morphism. Define a right action on $H$ by $x\cdot a=a^{-1}xF(a)$. The identities $x\cdot1=x$ and $(x\cdot a)\cdot b=(ab)^{-1}xF(ab)=x\cdot(ab)$ prove the action laws without commuting any factors. Equivalently $a\star x=x\cdot a^{-1}$ is a left action with the same orbits and stabilizers.

source.place: Paragraph before Definition 17.95, p.382, and first sentence of Theorem 17.96 proof, p.383.

proof.text: For each $x\in H(K)$ let $S_x$ be the scheme-theoretic stabilizer. Its $K$-points satisfy $a^{-1}xF(a)=x$, equivalently $xF(a)x^{-1}=a$. Thus [lem-sfb-inner-frobenius-fixed-points-finite] makes $S_x(K)$ finite. All hypotheses of [lem-sfb-zero-dimensional-stabilizer-finite-orbit] hold by step 1: $K$ is algebraically closed, the acting group $H$ is smooth connected affine of finite type, and its target $H$ is separated of finite type. Consequently $\dim S_x=0$; this implication does not assume that the stabilizer is reduced. Applying [lem-sfb-smooth-group-orbit-geometry] gives a locally closed reduced orbit $O_x$ with $\dim O_x=\dim H-\dim S_x=d$, and a surjective orbit map $H\to O_x$.

source.place: Theorem 17.96 and Corollary 17.97, printed p.383; Proposition 1.66, pp.27–28.

proof.text: Take the orbit $O_e$ of the identity. If its boundary $B=\overline{O_e}\setminus O_e$ were nonempty, it would contain a $K$-rational point $y$: the boundary is closed in $H$ because the orbit is locally closed and open in its closure; apply [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space] to this nonempty closed subset and [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base] to a closed point in it. By the boundary assertion of [lem-sfb-smooth-group-orbit-geometry], $\dim O_y<\dim O_e$. But step 3 gives both dimensions equal to $d$, a contradiction. Therefore $O_e$ is closed. It is irreducible, being the continuous image of irreducible $H$. If $O_e$ were a proper closed subset of $H$, any chain of irreducible closed subsets in $O_e$ could be extended by adjoining $H$; since $d$ is finite, this would give $\dim H\ge\dim O_e+1=d+1$. Thus $O_e=H$. This is the minimum-orbit/dimension argument of Milne, with all orbit dimensions already known to equal $d$.

source.place: Theorem 17.96 and Corollary 17.97, printed p.383; Proposition 1.66, pp.27–28.

proof.text: For $h\in H(K)$, step 3 and $O_e=H$ make the fibre of the orbit map $H\to H$, $a\mapsto a^{-1}F(a)$, over $h$ nonempty. It is of finite type over $K$: it is the closed subscheme cut out in affine finite-type $H$ by the coordinate equations $a^{-1}F(a)=h$, so its coordinate algebra is a quotient of a finitely generated $K$-algebra. It has a closed point by [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space], and that point has residue field $K$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base]. Its corresponding $g\in G(\bar k)$ satisfies $g^{-1}\sigma(g)=h$, as required. This step distinguishes surjectivity on scheme points from the asserted surjectivity on algebraic-closure-valued points.

source.place: Theorem 17.96 and Corollary 17.97, printed p.383; Proposition 1.66, pp.27–28.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q95-550476ea1 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read Milne iAG2017 p.382 (Frobenius on coordinates, before Def 17.95) and p.383 (Thm 17.96 proof, Cor 17.97). The item statement is unchanged and faithful: g^{-1}σ(g) is Milne's gF(g^{-1}) after g↦g^{-1}, σ is arithmetic Frobenius, and affineness is only a restriction of the source. Step 1: every citation checked. Geometric connectedness comes from the identity section, finite type from base change, smoothness from the lfp+flat point criterion (lfp is part of def-sbc-smooth), then separated, regular, integral (connected includes nonempty), and finite d from the identity local dimension. Step 2: genuinely elementary. The q-power map is a Hopf endomorphism in char p, it acts by σ on K-points, and the right-action law is verified; the left action has the same orbits and stabilizers. Step 3: the stabilizer is {a: xF(a)x^{-1}=a}. The new node gives finitely many K-points, the zero-dimensional-stabilizer node gives dim 0 (nonreduced stabilizers allowed), and the orbit node gives dim O_x=d. Step 4: the boundary is closed and has a K-point (Jacobson + rational closed points). It is invariant and its orbits have smaller dimension, contradicting d. So O_e is closed, and the chain argument with finite d gives O_e=H. Step 5: the fibre over h is a nonempty finite-type K-scheme, so it has a K-rational closed point. The left-action orbit map differs by the inversion automorphism; step 2 states that the orbits agree, which is acceptable. New node lem-sfb-inner-frobenius-fixed-points-finite: statement-only, self-contained and true. Milne's argument checks: f^j=Int(xσ(x)…σ^{j-1}(x))σ^j, y∈A(k_m) has finite order r, f^{mr}=σ^{mr}, so the fixed points lie in finite A(k_{mr}). Tested on G_a (u^q=u), G_m, finite constant groups and μ_p. It is strictly smaller than the item and is no duplicate: lem-sc-lang-steinberg is about vector spaces, thm-trf-frobenius-fixed-points is about untwisted fixed schemes, and the AV Lang unit is about abelian varieties. No cycle. The sole citer, finite-field-geometric-maximal-torus, is unaffected. The generic off-unit tool uses listed in split_report are accepted. Batch-5 flag: the cited lfp-smooth-flat-base-change node reaches lem-trf-smooth-at-point-fibre-criterion. That is the generic 01V9 fibre criterion, given by neither the trace-formula nor the Poincaré-duality assumption and no step of their proofs, so the citation is accepted. No changes.
